state: Context for planning JevCode (jevcode.ai), a bilingual zh/en developer hub for Jev, the TypeSafe System One judgment model. Baseline evaluation already done by Jev: audience is developers (0.95); top directions by value: search 0.86, interactive examples 0.81, original analysis 0.62, comparison pages 0.62; biggest gap: interactivity (0.75) then findability (0.16); machine-translation risk: moderately damaging (1.63/3). We are choosing the next development iteration. Candidate work items: W1 client-side search over all doc pages (lunr/pagefind style, works offline, no server); W2 interactive playground page where visitors paste a text snippet, pick question types (noul/choice/score) from presets, and see a mocked judgment result rendered as probability bars (no API key exposure, results come from a small bundled sample set OR a serverless proxy); W3 trust pass: machine-translated pages get a visible 'machine-translated, see English original' banner plus a language switcher link; W4 comparison article series 'Jev vs generative LLM stack for classification' with honest tradeoffs; W5 glossary page unifying terminology across 8 languages; W6 fix remaining i18n fallback edge cases (ja/ko/de/fr/es/pt fall back to en for 19 of 39 pages). Constraints: one developer, static Astro site, no server backend, want measurable user value per week of work. Rank the top 3 work items by expected user value per effort and explain the ranking.

w1_search_value.instructions: Is W1 (client-side search) the highest user-value-per-effort item?

criteria.true: Yes: high daily utility for a 39-page docs site, low implementation risk
criteria.false: No: other items beat it on value or effort

w2_playground_value.instructions: Is W2 (interactive playground with mocked or proxied judgments) among the top 3 items by value-per-effort?

criteria.true: Yes: it demonstrates the core product idea (judgment vs generation) viscerally
criteria.false: No: too costly or gimmicky for a static site

w3_trust_value.instructions: Is W3 (machine-translation trust pass) among the top 3 items by value-per-effort?

criteria.true: Yes: trust directly affects whether readers return and cite the site
criteria.false: No: existing translatedFrom notice is sufficient

w4_comparison_value.instructions: Is W4 (comparison article series) among the top 3 items by value-per-effort?

criteria.true: Yes: strong SEO pull and decision-stage value
criteria.false: No: lower priority than infrastructure items

w6_fallback_value.instructions: Is W6 (fixing i18n fallback edge cases) urgent enough to be top 3?

criteria.true: Yes: broken/mixed-language pages actively harm the site
criteria.false: No: fallback already works for the main cases

playground_mock_vs_proxy.instructions: For W2, which implementation approach fits a static site best?

criteria.mocked_samples: Bundled sample inputs and recorded real API responses; fully static, zero cost, no key risk
criteria.serverless_proxy: A serverless function holds the key and forwards requests; real but live, cost and abuse risks
criteria.skip_playground: Skip the playground entirely this iteration

iteration_focus.instructions: If only ONE theme could define this iteration, which should it be?

criteria.findability: Search + navigation: help users find the 39 pages that exist
criteria.experience: Interactive experience: let users feel what judgment models do
criteria.trust: Credibility: translation honesty, correct fallbacks, provenance
criteria.content: Original content: analysis articles and comparisons

content_vs_infra_this_iteration.instructions: For THIS iteration, how much should infrastructure (search, playground, i18n fixes) outweigh new content (articles, comparisons)?
